completion_vs_throughput_pilot.purpose: Separate fastest single completion from highest completed-games throughput without changing the global allocation or selecting a universal default count.
layouts: Oazis256x256 exactly eleven Nicowar FFA; no additional controller
completion_vs_throughput_pilot.seeds: Two fixed seeds per layout, exact controller count and initial save header/seed provenance sealed before launch. Reuse only verified eleven-Nicowar FFA saves; if two exact matching Oazis seeds are not already available, prepare and seal them explicitly. Never substitute the older observer workload.
gpu_strata: GPUon permitted; record actual field execution/commit/fallback/cancellation health
schedules: Serial batch: same two arrivals, one game at a time, each allowed total admitted participant allocationB including owner.
Concurrent batch: same two arrivals, two fixed disjoint masks partitioning exactlyB; per-game participants equal its allocated logical share.
completion_vs_throughput_pilot.arithmetic: 2layouts ×2GPUstrata ×2schedules ×2games =16 natural attempts. Counterbalance schedule order by layout/GPU; seed assignment and complete batch identities fixed.
completion_vs_throughput_pilot.allocation: Same caller-owned CPU-ID union and memory-planning total in both schedules; no compiling/profile/background jobs, no cpu mask based policy inference. Reserve OS capacity identically. GPU shared capacity is observed, not declared partitioned.
completion_vs_throughput_pilot.stopping: Winner or existing1hour per-game cap, preserving all censors. Batch makespan includes queues/startup; do not compute completed-game means with cap substituted or drop failed runs.
metrics: Per-game e2e and service wall separately; winner/ticks/status
Batch completedgames/makespan, all arrivals and unfinished work retained
Total waited-game user/systemCPU, CPU/tick and context switches/tick
Sum/concurrent peaks of native RSS or platformPSS, allocator/cache ownership and GPU memory where available
Cold startup versus retained process/cache state qualified; no pooling different envelopes
completion_vs_throughput_pilot.acceptance: Evaluate Pareto frontier: completion latency, batch throughput, total CPU, peak memory and correctness. Efficient-throughput must deliver credible throughput/resource benefit without hiding latency/censors; fast-simulation targets completion latency. Neither gains adoption solely by pooled mean or a selected seed. Pilot two seeds is descriptive; adopt only after replication across adverse layouts/devices and mature stages.
completion_vs_throughput_pilot.correctness: Use existing canonical diagnostics outside timed natural workloads; exact same-start per-tick GCS/world/RNG/replay and saved continuation. Never change simulation order, deadlines/publication, rules or features for the objective.
completion_vs_throughput_pilot.adoption_qualification: Sixteen attempts are a descriptive pilot and rejection screen only; insufficient to adopt calibrated profiles or general device thresholds.
